intro.title: Infinite Scroll
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that implements an infinite scroll feature, allowing users to load more content automatically as they scroll down a list. You will learn the core concept of detecting scroll events and conditionally triggering data fetches to simulate loading additional items. The main technologies involved include Angular's built-in directives, event handling, and TypeScript for managing state and logic. By the end, you'll have a working component that dynamically adds new items to a list, providing a seamless user experience common in modern web apps.
intro.usecase: Infinite scroll is a fundamental pattern in modern web applications where content loads continuously as users scroll down, eliminating the need for pagination buttons. You'll find this implemented in social media feeds like Facebook and Twitter, e-commerce product listings on Amazon, and content platforms like YouTube's video suggestions. As an Angular developer, you'll use infinite scroll to build data-heavy dashboards, news aggregators, or any interface where users browse through large datasets seamlessly. This pattern improves user experience by reducing initial load times while keeping engagement high through smooth, uninterrupted browsing.
